judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Memorandum repeatedly leans on the underlying CBA (e.g. §8.A wages, Appendix A.E pay entitlement, §7.C boards), so the boundary drawn here matters throughout; Appendix A.B.2's reference to "the current Collective Bargaining Agreement" expiring is in some tension with this extension to 2000.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An agreement to take "the steps necessary" to amend the plan is somewhat open but the object is identified by cross-reference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 3.A.(3) and the other H&W side letters; it presupposes rather than contradicts them.
judgments.clause_name: Side letter — Amendments to Health and Welfare Plan

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "On an inverse seniority basis, to assign the most junior qualified situation holder" and "pending final award" are workable, though "qualified" is undefined and the reach beyond Edison is unstated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits with Appendix A.C's inverse-seniority utilisation rule and with §4.D's bidding and consolidation rights, which govern the same vacancies from a different angle.
judgments.clause_name: Side letter — Filling vacant, newly created or temporary situations

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The last sentence — "They shall be permanently assigned to permanent or vacant positions in the event those situations are not filled by bid" — is loosely drafted and sits awkwardly with the preceding promise of restoration to the former situation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The same permanent-assignment rule appears again in the next paragraph together with the volunteer's return, so the two paragraphs overlap and must be sequenced by construction.
judgments.clause_name: Side letter — Notice to junior situation holders

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The interlocking three-day, seven-day and "not filled by bid" steps do not state how the volunteer's temporary fill relates to the bidding timetable, leaving the sequence uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates and partly restates the assignment rule in the preceding paragraph and interacts with §4.D's bidding rights, so the procedures must be harmonised.
judgments.clause_name: Side letter — Chapel Chairman notification procedure

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Foreseen to be of two (2) weeks or less duration" leaves the forecaster and the consequence of a mistaken forecast unstated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It carves out of the immediately preceding staffing procedures and is consistent with 4.C's relief from daily replacement.
judgments.clause_name: Side letter — Exclusion for short temporary vacancies

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, definite option keyed to assignments made under the same letter.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 4.D's discretion to fill or eliminate vacated situations; no conflict found.
judgments.clause_name: Side letter — Option to fill resulting vacancies

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "The NMDU may, within 72 hours, discuss the possibility of employment opportunities" creates no obligation on The Times and no consequence, so its operative effect is genuinely uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing else in the Memorandum addresses hiring from other papers, and §4.B channels RSH vacancies to Eligible Group I Employees, which limits any such opportunities.
judgments.clause_name: Side letter — Closure of Daily News or Post

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A specific award with named days off and a stated start time; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is an individual settlement and does not interact with the manning or bidding provisions in any contradictory way.
judgments.clause_name: Side letter — M. Santor grievance settlement (position awarded)

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Withdraw his grievance with prejudice" is definite and its consideration is stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the preceding paragraph and with the grievance machinery in §2.
judgments.clause_name: Side letter — M. Santor withdrawal of grievance
